title: Anthromes parameters

year.title: Year
year.description: The 75 HYDE 3.2 time steps: every thousand years to 0 AD, then every century, then every decade, then every year from 2000. HYDE 3.2's input grids end at 2017.

color_by.title: Color by
color_by.description: The anthrome class; the used fraction of each cell; whether each cell has people at or above the wild cutoff; population density; or where this classification differs from the same method run at native resolution before aggregation.

used_threshold.title: Used-land threshold
used_threshold.description: The share of a cell's land that must be cropped, grazed or built before a remote or uninhabited cell counts as used. Published value 20%. It applies only in the two lowest population bands. In denser cells, the cropland and grazing thresholds decide on their own.

crops_threshold.title: Cropland threshold
crops_threshold.description: The share of a cell that must be cropland before the cell is a cropland anthrome. Published value 20%.

grazing_threshold.title: Grazing threshold
grazing_threshold.description: The share of a cell that must be pasture or rangeland before the cell is a grazing anthrome. Published value 20%. The reference code keeps it separate from the cropland threshold.

rice_threshold.title: Rice threshold
rice_threshold.description: In cells above the dense settlement density, the share of irrigated rice that makes the cell a rice village. Published value 20%.

irrigation_threshold.title: Irrigation threshold
irrigation_threshold.description: The irrigated share that separates irrigated villages and residential irrigated croplands from their rainfed versions. Published value 20%.

urban_fraction_threshold.title: Urban area threshold
urban_fraction_threshold.description: The built-up share that makes a cell urban, whatever its population. Published value 20%.

urban_density.title: Urban density
urban_density.description: People per km² of land above which a cell is urban, whatever its built-up area. Published value 2,500.

dense_settlement_density.title: Dense settlement density
dense_settlement_density.description: The lower edge of the dense settlement and village band. Below it, a cell cannot be a village. Published value 100.

residential_density.title: Residential density
residential_density.description: The lower edge of the residential band: residential croplands, rangelands and woodlands. Published value 10.

populated_density.title: Populated density
populated_density.description: The line between populated and remote. Below it, a cropland is a remote cropland. Published value 1.

wild_density.title: Wild cutoff
wild_density.description: The population density below which a cell counts as uninhabited, and so wild. Published value 0.0001 people per km², one person per 10,000 km², a rule in the reference code rather than the paper. The inhabited land view draws this line. If it reaches the populated density, the remote classes are empty.

tree_biomes.title: Forested biomes
tree_biomes.description: How many of the fifteen potential vegetation classes count as forested. The classes run from tropical evergreen forest to polar ice, and the published cascade draws the line after class 8. It decides whether seminatural and wild cells are woodland or dryland.

$comment: Slider granularity is x-step, never multipleOf - see bathtub's schema for why. The year is an enum of 75 HYDE time steps drawn as a slider over the stop index (x-control: slider); the value stays the enum member so validation is unchanged. Property order is the panel's reading order: the clock and the view, then the six land-use thresholds with the used-land one first, then the five density cutoffs with the wild cutoff last, then the one vegetation control. The wild cutoff is a numeric enum drawn as a slider (x-control: slider), so it moves in four fixed steps.
